scenario.title: Dependencies and related projects
situations: One change must wait for another to merge or become live.
Two independent edits share files without needing execution order.
A reusable producer change must be proved against a consuming project.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Traced intake and displayed graph semantics; multi-project runtime and exact candidate verification are not independently revalidated here.
How should the human discover an existing related project without authorizing unrelated writes?
Command nodes, when present, were checked with installed CLI --help only; this proves parser/help availability, not serving-control-plane capability or successful execution.

lessons.title: Name the real wait
lessons.when: When a user or agent identifies a prerequisite at start, integration, delivery or closeout.
lessons.need: Dependencies can gate starting, merging or closing; the condition may be item completion, merge or delivery to a named environment. Coordination-only overlap creates no wait.
lessons.surface: Intake dependency inference; Frontier reason text and dependency detail
lessons.gap: Review question: should JOURNEYS teach the actual wait when the user states it, rather than expose every edge type up front?

lessons.title: Keep project ownership separate
lessons.when: When the requested outcome touches multiple project repositories or changes a reusable producer contract.
lessons.need: Each project retains its own item and lane; companion items express a real cross-project dependency and exact consumer proof. Related does not automatically mean shared deployment.
lessons.surface: Intake cross-project handling; project/document steering scope
lessons.gap: JOURNEYS 14 says link them but lacks a beginner procedure. Review question: should its guide distinguish shared context, dependent work and shared delivery as separate needs?
